content:
In #37346 there's been some discussion with @Michael Rothgang and @Filippo A. E. Nuccio on if simp should be squeezed when followed by grind.

Filippo's argument in favor of squeezing as I understand is essentially that a simp; grind proof could be unstable when adding new simp annotations. My thought was that in practice that we add these annotations in pairs of @[simp, grind =], so that they are designed to capture the same equivalence class. My intuition had been that grind would likely be more incomplete for the foreseeable future, but was being added in a fashion compatible with simp and this is why we considered it flexible.

I think it would be helpful to discuss the following:

  • Most concretely, do people think that grind should be considered flexible by the linter? This has been the case since #29027 was merged in September
  • How should simp and grind = annotations align? Are there any situations where we don't want both? Is my intuition that it is bad if grind equivalence classes diverge from simp normal forms widely held?

My take here is that grind being considered flexible is dependent on this compatibility of annotations, which seems like a good idea to me that has already been implicitly happening (and perhaps is possible to environment lint against similar to simpNF?)

Just to add a word to @Chris Henson 's summary (which is perfectly accurate) is that I believe that in the long run we need grind and simp to be properly aligned, but this is not the case now and it is not actually required in new PR's. My suggestion is to keep simp squeezed when followed by grind until we agree on a more stable strategy and uniform requirements in new PR's
Yes, I think we agree on the long run behavior and more uniform reviewing/linting! I'm just not sure about considering grind rigid in the meantime.

I'd agree with @Chris Henson here. In fact, if there is a situation where a simp; grind call breaks, then I think this is a useful signal to whoever caused this breakage: in that case they should probably reconsider which simp/grind tags they are adding/removing.

Although I understand the point, I fear that this might not be very efficient if less experienced people try to contribute, since they would simply face a broken grind (not a broken simp) after they add a simp lemma. Perhaps it would be useful also to add to the discussion what the benefits of avoiding squeezing simps would be.

#mathlib4 > request: discourage squeezing terminal simps?
#mathlib4 > linter requests @ 💬
#36728

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Perhaps it would be useful also to add to the discussion what the benefits of avoiding squeezing simps would be.

My answer would be that the benefits are the exact same as when grind is uninvolved, plus Jovan's explanation. Building Mathlib with grind no longer marked as flexible, I count 218 occurrences of unsquzeed simp; grind. So probably not enough signal to know how stable these proofs are in practice

Snir Broshi said:

#mathlib4 > request: discourage squeezing terminal simps?
#mathlib4 > linter requests @ 💬
#36728

I'm very very well aware of all that discussion but it was related to terminal simps, which are similar but not identical to simps followed by flexible tactics and the level of "flexibility" of grind is something's which has been discussed but not really decided.

Just for the context, here my example:

import Mathlib

def b : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
def c : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
def a : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
def f : ℕ → ℕ := sorry

@[grind]
lemma foo1 (n : ℕ) : a n = b n := sorry

@[simp]
lemma foo2 (n : ℕ) : c n = b n := sorry

example : f (a 3) = f (c 3) := by simp; grind
where adding simp to the annotation of foo1 breaks the proof of the example.

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

I'm very very well aware of all that discussion but it was related to terminal simps, which are similar but not identical to simps followed by flexible tactics and the level of "flexibility" of grind is something's which has been discussed but not really decided.

I think there is still a misunderstanding here. The current style guide says:

terminal simp calls (a simp call is terminal if it closes the current goal or is only followed by flexible tactics such as ring, field_simp, aesop) should not be squeezed

This is clearly written to include simp followed by flexible tactics to mean "terminal", not just calls to simp that are syntactically the last tactic closing a goal. That this was surprising to some, including experienced maintainers, is what prompted continued discussion in those threads.

Of course the style guide can be changed if this is a misrepresentation of what is wanted for Mathlib, but there are examples in the linked threads like simp; ring that people seem to agree we don't want to squeeze. If we apply this consistently to everything currently marked flexible, simp; grind shouldn't be squeezed either. (Again, I am outlaying what seems to be a straightforward reading of the docs, not putting this forth as absolute truth)
I would also think that simp; grind or simp; ring should be allowed.

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Snir Broshi said:

#mathlib4 > request: discourage squeezing terminal simps?
#mathlib4 > linter requests @ 💬
#36728

I'm very very well aware of all that discussion but it was related to terminal simps, which are similar but not identical to simps followed by flexible tactics and the level of "flexibility" of grind is something's which has been discussed but not really decided.

I was responding to this message of yours:
Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Perhaps it would be useful also to add to the discussion what the benefits of avoiding squeezing simps would be.

This is exactly what you asked for.

Joël Riou said:

I would also think that simp; grind or simp; ring should be allowed.

As a matter of fact since grind calls ring the second is a special case of the first, no?
No, grind does not call ring. Rather, grind has its own algebraic solver.
I agree, technically, but it seems to me to be a special case of the other in terms of flexibility.

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Although I understand the point, I fear that this might not be very efficient if less experienced people try to contribute, since they would simply face a broken grind (not a broken simp) after they add a simp lemma. Perhaps it would be useful also to add to the discussion what the benefits of avoiding squeezing simps would be.

I think this is the key point here - we all agree that simp; grind should eventually be allowed (encouraged?). However, while we don't have alignment between simp and grind, the underlying problem with non-terminal simp (it can lead to breakage in proofs in tricky ways) remains present, and may be hit by less experienced people.

My personal opinion is that this is not likely to happen very often, and even then will happen mostly in CI rather than local builds, at which point a contributor may ask a more experienced person for help (and we'll get the correct new grind lemma). However the point remains that the flexibility of simp is not always matched by the flexibility of grind, so eg with the current grind set, a simp; grind proof is more likely to break by simp; aesop.
